name: Alison Cockburn
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Alison Cockburn (née Rutherford) was a Scottish society hostess in Edinburgh, a friend of Hume, Scott and Burns, and the author of one of the best-known versions of The Flowers of the Forest.
Gilfillan prints her version, which opens 'I've seen the smiling', beside the older version by Jean Elliot.

poems.title: The Flowers of the Forest
poems.author: Alison Cockburn
poems.collection: Specimens with Memoirs of the Less-known British Poets, ed. George Gilfillan (1860)
poems.text:
I've seen the smiling
Of Fortune beguiling;
I've felt all its favours, and found its decay:
Sweet was its blessing,
Kind its caressing;
But now 'tis fled--fled far away.

I've seen the forest
Adorned the foremost
With flowers of the fairest most pleasant and gay;
Sae bonnie was their blooming!
Their scent the air perfuming!
But now they are withered and weeded away.

I've seen the morning
With gold the hills adorning,
And loud tempest storming before the mid-day.
I've seen Tweed's silver streams,
Shining in the sunny beams,
Grow drumly and dark as he rowed on his way.

Oh, fickle Fortune,
Why this cruel sporting?
Oh, why still perplex us, poor sons of a day?
Nae mair your smiles can cheer me,
Nae mair your frowns can fear me;
For the Flowers of the Forest are a' wede away.
